solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Distinguish between two types of split

definitions.meaning: to tell two things from each other is to discriminate or differentiate them
split in the sense of inform on someone (tell, as a grass does) followed by split in the sense of separated or asunder (apart)

explanation.walkthrough: The second half works as two meanings of 'split' laid end to end: to split on someone is to tell, and things that have split are apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to differentiate two similar things is exactly what the phrase means: you can discriminate one from the other.

clue.text: Can hosts become cross?

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: a can is a tin
to go is to become, as in going mad

explanation.surface: A question about whether a tin can turn angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, but it is a noun: a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid offspring of a tiger and a lioness is a cross between two big-cat species.

clue.text: If you fancy this setter, you may also have to tolerate a different one!

definitions.text: If you fancy this setter, you may also have to tolerate a different one!

parts.words: If you fancy this setter, you may also have to tolerate a different one
parts.note: the setter of the puzzle is also, in another sense, a breed of dog (an Irish or English setter), so loving the setter brings a canine along too

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says that loving someone means accepting all that comes with them, their pet included. 'setter' is both the crossword compiler and a gundog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb means that affection for a person obliges you to accept their faults and attachments as well.

clue.text: Selflessness that's really at heart platitude

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, so only the middle letters of really are used

parts.note: a platitude is a truism, a statement too obvious to be worth making

explanation.surface: A cynic's view that unselfishness is, deep down, just a tired cliché.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is concern for others' welfare above one's own, which is selflessness by another name.

clue.text: Jump with blade to cut line

parts.note: an axe is a bladed tool for chopping

explanation.surface: A skater leaps with a blade slicing across a marked line on the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The skating blade in the surface is a red herring: the blade wanted is a chopping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a figure-skating leap with a forward take-off and one and a half turns in the air.

clue.text: Cheering cup fan's taken ride around, close to skipper

indicators.note: around here means turned about and rearranged, so these letters are shuffled
the close of a word is its end, so the last letter of skipper is taken

explanation.surface: A supporter celebrating a trophy win goes for a ride with the team captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheering cup' recalls Cowper's line about 'the cups that cheer but not inebriate', meaning tea; the 's of 'fan's' means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen on the cheering cup is one who loves a brew of the leaf from China and India.

clue.text: Fed on fabrication that concludes the debate!

indicators.note: a fabrication is something made up or constructed, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A rebuttal that ends an argument rests on nothing but invention.
explanation.walkthrough: The colloquial exclamation 'End of!' is short for 'end of story' or 'end of discussion'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clipped exclamation is said to close an argument: nothing more to discuss, the matter is settled.

clue.text: Are Leavers not disheartened by Britain's future status?

parts.note: after Brexit Britain would be ex-EU, no longer in the European Union

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of not is removed

explanation.surface: A Brexit question: are Leave voters still cheerful about the country's prospects?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leavers' suggests Brexit voters, but the definition is a stage direction meaning 'they go off'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin stage direction tells several actors to depart, so it says that they leave the stage.

clue.text: Entirely because of article, crushed

parts.note: down to means owing to, as in 'it was down to luck'
the is the definite article
ground means crushed to powder, as coffee beans are

explanation.surface: Something was totally destroyed by a newspaper story.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely or perfectly, as in 'that suits me' in every respect.

clue.text: Smart Kensington postcode written in letters for boxer

parts.note: fly is slang for sharp or knowing
Kensington in London has the postcode W8; spelled out in words that is W and eight

explanation.surface: A stylish address in an upmarket London district, spelled out on an envelope for a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensington is a wealthy district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a boxer in the lightest standard division of the sport, so a fighter of that class.

clue.text: Generous grouse shooter may squeal

definitions.meaning: a generous shooter might hand the birds bagged (the game) to others
to squeal is to reveal a secret, to blab

explanation.walkthrough: Game here is shot birds such as grouse; the idiom is to reveal a secret by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting slip a secret plan, as an informer who blabs does, is the meaning of the idiom.

clue.text: Ring back in no more than fifty-nine seconds?

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: under a minute is sub-minute, written SUB plus MIN, the usual abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: Getting a call returned within a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring back' looks like returning a phone call, but 'back' is the reversal signal and 'Ring' is a halo.
explanation.definitionFit: A luminous halo around the head of a saint in art is also called by this word.

clue.text: Not fair when superior virtually eclipses career

indicators.note: to eclipse is to cover, so one word surrounds another
virtually means almost, so the last letter of the word for superior is dropped

parts.note: better means superior
to career is to run headlong

explanation.surface: A worker unfairly passed over when a boss nearly overshadows their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims BETTER to BETTE, which then surrounds RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair describes blond hair; someone dark-haired is therefore not fair.

clue.text: What's contained in chemical it must establish?

definitions.text: What's contained in chemical it must establish?

indicators.note: the letters wanted are held within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A question about what a chemical reagent is meant to prove.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a chemical test that must establish acidity or alkalinity.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive trial that settles a question, originally the chemical one showing acid or alkali by colour change.

clue.text: People written to no longer having to stop new casino

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece goes into the gap of the other
new means remade, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: loss is the state of no longer having something

explanation.surface: A gambler, no longer flush, has to quit a newly opened casino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the casino letters into COIANS, and 'to stop' plugs the gap after the first two. 'People written to' is the Bible's epistle title, not ordinary correspondents.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul's epistle was addressed to the Christians of Colossae, so they are recipients of a biblical letter.

clue.text: Material appeared hard in earth

parts.note: came means appeared or arrived

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for hard inside the word for earth

parts.note: an earth is a fox's den, a lair
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Some fabric turned up, stiff, buried in the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth' is not soil but an animal's den.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft fabric woven from the coat of a dromedary or Bactrian, used in coats.

clue.text: Short step for man

indicators.note: short means cut, so the last letter of the word for step is dropped

parts.note: a stage is a step in a process

explanation.surface: A brief stride for a person, recalling the first moon landing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'one small step for man'. As an adjective, stag means for men only, as in a stag party.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag do or stag night is for the males only, so the word stands for men or a man.

clue.text: Note in contract for firing agent

indicators.note: in puts the musical note inside the word for contract

parts.note: to contract an illness is to pick it up
me (or mi) is the third note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A clause in an employment contract allows a staff agency to sack someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing' suggests dismissal, but means firing someone up, rousing them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic or stimulating drink revives and energises, firing a person up.

clue.text: Stratagem an instant success in WWII

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
VE stands for Victory in Europe, the Allied triumph of May 1945

explanation.surface: A clever plan won quickly during the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactical step or manoeuvre in a game or scheme is a ploy, a stratagem.

clue.text: Let one quite quietly correct grasping people

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
mp, mezzo piano, is the musical direction for moderately quiet

indicators.note: grasping means holding, so the word for correct goes round the word for people

parts.note: to edit is to correct text
men are people

explanation.surface: Allow someone to set greedy people straight in a gentle voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' is the noun in 'without let or hindrance', not the verb meaning allow.
explanation.definitionFit: A let is an obstruction or hindrance, as in a legal phrase or a tennis serve that is replayed.

clue.text: Mysterious spot round well bores

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so these letters go inside the word for spot

parts.note: to spot is to see, to spy
O is round in shape
OK means well or all right

explanation.surface: A strange place near a water well where drilling goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie or uncanny, suggestive of ghosts, seems mysterious.

clue.text: Following punch, after something for leaning on, by George!

definitions.text: something for leaning on, by George

indicators.note: after places the word for following behind the word for punch

parts.note: lamp is slang for hit or punch
post as a prefix means following or later

explanation.surface: Someone recovers from a blow by holding something steady, with a mild oath.
explanation.walkthrough: George Formby, the British comic singer, had a hit with 'Leaning on a Lamp-post'; 'by George!' is also an old exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: In George Formby's song the singer props himself against a street light while waiting for his girl.

clue.text: Avoids runners, keeping right

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the word for runners goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: skis are runners, as on a sledge

explanation.surface: Someone sidesteps athletes who stay on the right side of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt an issue is to go round its edge rather than tackle it, so to evade it.

clue.text: Go up with champ at last for European trophy

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: to scale is to climb or go up

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of champ

explanation.surface: A winner climbs the podium for a continental cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the E of SCALE for P.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalp, taken from a defeated enemy, was a trophy, hence any prize won from an opponent.

clue.text: Capital city of this country backed by its airline

parts.note: BA is British Airways, the UK's flag carrier

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the abbreviation for this country is read in reverse

parts.note: for a British newspaper this country is the UK

explanation.surface: A capital city supported by the national airline of the country it is in.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Azerbaijan, on the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: Adorable plays with unnamed stars

indicators.note: plays means fools around with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sweet anonymous performer acts alongside the big names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' looks like the actors in the surface, but means a galaxy.
explanation.definitionFit: This galaxy, the nearest large spiral to the Milky Way, is a vast collection of stars.

clue.text: Doctor close to Eleanor?

parts.note: to rig is to doctor or tamper with
by means near or beside

explanation.surface: A question about a physician being near a woman called Eleanor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles song title 'Eleanor Rigby' puts the surname right beside Eleanor, so the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Beatles song the lonely woman's surname follows her first name, so it sits right beside Eleanor.

clue.text: Endlessly proclaim Irish politicians fake

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter of the word for proclaim is dropped

parts.note: to trumpet is to proclaim loudly
the DUP, Democratic Unionist Party, is a Northern Irish political party

explanation.surface: Accusing Northern Irish politicians of endless phoney proclamations.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumped-up charge is invented or falsified, so it is fake.
